What are your tips for driving in snow?

Leave extra early so you can go slowly and safely the whole way. Do not be tempted to speed up even if the road appears clear because it only takes one patch of black ice to ruin your ride.

Source: was commercial truck driver for 10 years.
My friend made this mistake a few years ago and spun into a fire hydrant. Mustang was totaled and the entire street had to be shut down.

Agreed, only time I lost control was when I relaxed and went too fast

NEVER RELAX GUYS

Put some weight in your vehicle. A couple of sandbags is enough for most pickup trucks. Like 600 lbs or so is good. Most people don't use enough weight.

Don't completely stop if you can help it, might not be legal but you have much better control at intersections.

Get actual snow tires, all season tires aren't good for most winter conditions.

If you see a stop sign, start slowing down as soon as you see it. If it is a two way stop and you don't have a stop sign, slow down because others might not. Even if you aren't at fault when you hit someone, standing out in the cold while waiting for the cops and a tow truck isn't fun.

Biggest tip, don't panic. If you are going slow enough and bump another car, there probably won't be much damage. As soon as you panic, you'll do something crazy and the hit will be much worse.
Weigh down your car a bit if you can.

Go slow. That's about it. That and brake before you hit snow and ice patches, not when you're on them. It's really not hard or dangerous if you god damn go slow. I don't why that's so hard for people. Conversely, if you are in deep snow, don't let off the gas, keep going.

Having 20 years experience on non-salted roads and places that will be 1 foot of pure ice.

  1. Buy Bridgestone Blizzak tires!

  2. Drive slower and start breaking way earlier

  3. Never ever fucking tailgate!!

  4. Don't think ABS will ever do anything for you. I've taken my fuse out in a couple of cars.

  5. Learn to pump your break instead of a normal push. This prevents your breaks from locking and the abs from engaging.

  6. Learn that curves will push you outward / inward just because they are icey.

  7. Bigger and heavier vehicles slide farther. Little 1000cc things actually stop pretty quick.

  8. Rear wheel drive cars will kick out because people are stupid and can't drive.

  9. Front wheel cars, you'll get shitty traction and will need to rock your steering wheel left - right to get gripe.

  10. Don't jack rabbit start. You'll just spin your tires.

The only advice anyone who sucks at driving in the snow will be able to understand is to go slow and make maneuvers as gradual as possible. Anybody interested should read about Third Places.

Basically the Third Space is a place apart from your home and work. For a community to succeed the third place must have certain properties. Some of these are severely lacking in what we have today.

It be free to access for everybody i.e. it can't be Starbucks or the mall. It has to be public space where you can go to hang out without spending money. It must not limit access to only certain type of people, so a biker bar is no good also. A park is a good candidate.

Food and drink are ok but not essential. When you sit at the cafe at the square you have to order something, can't just sit there so it is no good. It is very important that the food and drink sales are not monopolized. In other words sitting at the town square and buying drinks from the shop at the corner is ok but not ideal because it limits the choice to only those shops close to the square.

It must be highly accessible by foot and other types of transport. Must be close to schools and public buildings.

Must be neutral ground. No affiliation to party or business. No sponsorships. No ads. No religion.

Must involve locals and regulars. A highly touristic places are not ideal.

Must be low key and welcoming. Conversation is main activity but can also accommodate sports and performances.

Etc. etc. Read more at the wiki page. If still interested watch this.

TL;DR - Shops and businesses have been chipping and undermining third spaces since forever and today there are no third places left. No wonder people are no longer going to the shops buying things. The main point of going out has been eroded away.
